english: My grandfather, where are the stars by day? -- Child, they are in the sky; the sun hides them. -- Is the sun stronger than the stars? -- It is stronger. The stars shine at night. -- Do you see all of them? -- I do not see all with my eyes; my eyes are tired. -- Now the stars watch you from below/under them.
uncertain: ḱm̥h₂tā́m: read as 'tired' (ḱemh₂-) but case/gender unclear

english: Brother, at night I do not see the moon. -- A cloud covers it. Soon it rains. -- Now drive the sheep home. -- We drive them. Where is your dog? -- It lies near the fire. The dog is heavy/slow. -- Lead it there.

What did you have in mind? -- I think of the full moon. I count the winters by its light. -- Will you lead me with you? -- I lead you if you are silent. -- I am silent, I do not speak. -- Now we go under the night.
uncertain: h₂éwh₂e: unsure of this verb; maybe 'see/perceive' perfect 2sg

english: When do we worship the king's gods? -- When the new moon is born. Now the year turns and the days become long. -- What do I bring? -- Bring a white sheep and milk. -- I bring those. Will you pour mead? -- I pour it and we sing to Sky.

Sister, a star fell from the sky. -- Where did it fall? -- Into the river. Now a great man has died; my grandfather said that. -- Is that true? -- I do not know. The gods know it. -- Was the star bright? -- It was white and swift.

The sun warms the stone; we sit. We sit under the tree. -- Are you thirsty? -- I am thirsty; give me water. -- Drink. -- Now the days are long. When the sun sets, we go home. Now in the evening we drink mead.
